Art style: clean modern visual-novel illustration. Establishing shot of Halcyon Reach. The Halcyon family seat, a Loomwright-inclined house of pale terraces and glass conservatories perched above the cloudlanes, indigo-and-silver thread in every hanging. Art style: clean modern visual-novel illustration. Establishing shot of Execution Square. A public plaza built for the display of state power: a broad flagged square hemmed by government facades, a raised iron scaffold at its heart, broadcast-horns and scrying-plates mounted high so the whole quarter can be made to watch. Assayer grey and governmental brass. Crowd-barriers, banners of a hostile regime, and the cold theatrical lighting of a place designed so that punishment is never private. In daylight it is grimly ordinary; lit for an execution it becomes the stage on which the story's cruelty is made undeniable. Time of day / condition: day. No characters, no text.

Art style: clean modern visual-novel illustration. Character portrait of Caedon Vale. A nineteen-year-old scholarship student at the Cog-College of Cograuncy, born to a Ferran furnace-town family of modest means. Caedon is lean and wiry from years hauling coke on the furnace floors, with dark tousled hair, storm-grey eyes, and a smear of engine soot that never quite washes out from under his nails. He carries himself with a watchful, self-taught steadiness — the wariness of someone who has always been the outsider in a room of guild-born peers. Unusually, Caedon draws on both Currents — a faint pull of ordered Sela and wild Vash alike — a rarity the College has not yet decided whether to prize or fear. He channels without a Governor by instinct, which terrifies his professors and thrills the Kiln-Sworn recruiters. Earnest, stubborn, and quick to defend those the guild-state overlooks, he is the still point around whom the other students orbit. Palette: #2b2f36, #8a6a4f, #b8b0a4, #6d7681, #c9772f. Neutral pose and expression, plain neutral background, head-and-shoulders framing.

Art style: clean modern visual-novel illustration. Character portrait of Ember Kellan. A Kiln-Sworn forge-prodigy from the Vashan Dominion, Ember is Vash-strong and channels raw, ungoverned current with a reckless brilliance that terrifies her instructors. Broad-shouldered and sun-dark, with close-cropped copper hair and the first faint rust-scarring already tracing her right forearm — a mark she wears like a dare. She grew up in Cinderhold's forge-quarters, tending engine-fires before she could read, and came to the Cog-College half as a prodigy and half as a Dominion test of whether their heresy could be tamed by Ferran licensing. It cannot. Hot-tempered, loyal, and allergic to caution, she believes power is meant to be spent, not metered — and privately fears how little time the Rust will leave her. Beneath the swagger is someone who loves fiercely because she does not expect to love long. Palette: #c8531b, #e8912d, #3a2418, #8a8175. Art style: Japanese anime. Establishing shot of Dormitory Commons. A cluttered common room in the student stacks: mismatched armchairs, a coal hearth under a copper hood, a long scarred table strewn with study-cogs, playing cards, and half-drunk tea. This is where the wider friend group forms, and where students, including Caedon and his male cohort, can let their guards down, building the ensemble who will crew the ruins test and, later, become stranded pairs. Art style: Japanese anime. Establishing shot of Execution Square. A public plaza built for the display of state power: a broad flagged square hemmed by government facades, a raised iron scaffold at its heart, broadcast-horns and scrying-plates mounted high so the whole quarter can be made to watch. Assayer grey and governmental brass dominate the architecture. Crowd-barriers, banners of a hostile regime, and the cold theatrical lighting create a stage where punishment is never private. Mood: ominous, oppressive, public. Time of day / condition: day. Palette: #55524c, #8d8a81, #1f1c1a, #7a1f1f. No characters, no text.

Scrubbed open country on the marches of the Vashan Dominion — red dust, wind-carved rock, dead telegraph lines, and no forge for a hundred miles to shelter a Kiln-Sworn. Art style: Japanese anime. Establishing shot of The Grey Principality of Vorn. A cold northern principality of grey stone and iron: cliff-perched devotional houses, bell-towers, and shrine-roads where the Assayers' writ runs absolute and channeling is leashed to piety. Fog rolls off slate seas; everything is scrubbed, ordered, and watched. It is Isolde's homeland and her cage — the place whose devotional networks and Assayer methods she knows well enough to keep them both alive, even as the truth they uncover implicates the very order she was raised to serve. The executed pair lands on her here like a verdict on her own faith. Mood: austere, devout, cold. Time of day / condition: day. Palette: #6b7686, #d7dce2, #2f3540, #8fa8c4. No characters, no text.

Art style: Japanese anime. Establishing shot of The Ruins (Exterior). A field of collapsed aetherwork on a wind-scoured moor beyond the cloudlanes: toppled clocktower drums, a fallen furnace-spine gone green with corrosion, viaduct arches broken off into open sky. Old Governors lie half-buried and cold, and a faint teal residue still weeps from cracked conduits where a great weaving once failed. Silent but for wind and the tick of settling metal, it is exactly the kind of place a field-test is set — and exactly the kind of place an ambush hides. This is where the cohort is assigned to investigate, building tension towards the inevitable intervention of nefarious actors. Mood: eerie, abandoned, tense. Time of day / condition: day. Art style: Japanese anime. Establishing shot of The Grey Hands' Assay-Hold. A nineteen-year-old scholarship student at the Cog-College of Cograuncy, born to a Ferran furnace-town family of modest means. Caedon is lean and wiry from years hauling coke on the furnace floors, with dark tousled hair, storm-grey eyes, and a smear of engine soot that never quite washes out from under his nails. He carries himself with a watchful, self-taught steadiness — the wariness of someone who has always been the outsider in a room of guild-born peers. Unusually, Caedon draws on both Currents — a faint pull of ordered Sela and wild Vash alike — a rarity the College has not yet decided whether to prize or fear. He channels without a Governor by instinct, which terrifies his professors and thrills the Kiln-Sworn recruiters. Earnest, stubborn, and quick to defend those the guild-state overlooks, he is the still point around whom the other students orbit. Palette: #2b2f36, #8a6a4f, #b8b0a4, #6d7681, #c9772f. Preserve the exact face and look from the reference image. Headmistress of the Cog-College, a woman in her late fifties who wears authority like a well-oiled mechanism. Auria rose through the Regulen Concord as a Sela-strong administrator rather than a battle-channeler, and she runs the College the way the Ferran Ascendancy likes its institutions run: metered, licensed, and accountable. Silver hair coiled tight beneath a brass circlet, a high slate-and-white coat of office, and a Governor gauntlet she rarely needs but always wears as a symbol. She is shrewd, fair, and quietly political — she must keep Concord inspectors, Dominion recruiters, and half a dozen monarchies' heirs all under one roof without the place burning down. Beneath the protocol is genuine care for her students and an old, private doubt about what the Assayers do with those the College severs. Palette: #5a6472, #f2f0ea, #b08d55, #2b2f36. Professor Mirabel Quist is the Cog-College's mistress of Governors — the artificer-scholar who teaches the theory and craft of the brass-and-crystal regulators that meter a channeler's flow. A wiry woman in her fifties with cropped iron-grey hair, ink-stained fingers, and a jeweler's loupe forever pushed up on her forehead, she moves through her workshop amid a clutter of half-built gauntlets, crystal blanks, and pressure gauges. Sela-strong and Concord-trained, she believes fervently that measured power is the only safe power, yet she is no dogmatist: she quietly studies the failures of Governors, including the ones the Concord would rather bury. Warm, blunt, and endlessly curious, she treats students as apprentices and machines as puzzles. She is the professor most likely to notice when a student's talent outruns their Governor — and the one who understands exactly how dangerous that is. Palette: #b08d57, #d8d8d8, #3a4a5a, #7a6a55. Full-body front view of Silas Thorn wearing A slate-grey Cog-College master's gown over a high-collared brass-buttoned waistcoat, a licensed Governor gauntlet locked to his left forearm, acid-stained gloves tucked at his belt.. Preserve the exact face and look from the reference image. A gaunt, severe man in his late fifties, Professor Silas Thorn teaches the theory and discipline of Governors at the Cog-College — the brass-and-crystal regulators that meter a channeler's flow. Ferran to the bone and a devoted man of the Regulen Concord, he believes utterly that only measured power is safe power, and he drills that creed into every student who passes through his laboratory. His long fingers are stained with crystal-etching acid and his forearm bears a licensed Governor he has never once removed in public. Thorn is exacting, cold, and quietly brilliant; he has forgotten more about the mechanics of the Weave than most channelers ever learn. Beneath the rigor is an old grief — a former student who burned out under his instruction — that he has sealed away behind procedure. He distrusts the Kiln-Sworn as heretics and the Ashen Circle as criminals, and he watches any student who leans toward raw Vash with the wariness of a man who has seen where it ends. A gaunt, severe man in his late fifties, Professor Silas Thorn teaches the theory and discipline of Governors at the Cog-College — the brass-and-crystal regulators that meter a channeler's flow. Ferran to the bone and a devoted man of the Regulen Concord, he believes utterly that only measured power is safe power, and he drills that creed into every student who passes through his laboratory. His long fingers are stained with crystal-etching acid and his forearm bears a licensed Governor he has never once removed in public. Thorn is exacting, cold, and quietly brilliant; he has forgotten more about the mechanics of the Weave than most channelers ever learn. Beneath the rigor is an old grief — a former student who burned out under his instruction — that he has sealed away behind procedure. He distrusts the Kiln-Sworn as heretics and the Ashen Circle as criminals, and he watches any student who leans toward raw Vash with the wariness of a man who has seen where it ends.
